Important note: To prepare lemongrass tea at home, obtain lemongrass stalks from a nursery store, and plant them in a sunny area with well-drained soil. Keep the soil moist and trim the stalks regularly for fresh leaves, perfect for brewing homemade lemongrass tea.

Important note: To prepare Tulsi tea and plant a Tulsi plant at home, just sow Tulsi seeds in a sunny spot with well-draining soil, water regularly, and pluck the leaves for brewing when they're mature.
Important Note: Eat until you reach satiety, ensuring you consume enough food to satisfy your hunger and nutritional needs.

recipes.name: Option 1 : Drumstick leaves Kashayam
steps: Take ½ fistful of drumstick leaves
and wash well.
Then take 200 ml of water and let it boil.
Add the washed drumstick leaves
in the boiling water and wait for 5 minutes.
Then filter and have it empty stomach

recipes.name: Option 2: Tulsi (Holy Basil) Leaf Kashayam
steps: Take a handful of Tulsi (Holy Basil) leaves and wash them thoroughly.
Boil 200 ml of water.
Add the washed Tulsi leaves to the boiling water.
Let it boil/steep for 3–4 minutes.
Strain and drink it on an empty stomach.

recipes.name: Option 3: Coriander Leaf Kashayam
steps: Take a handful of coriander leaves and wash them thoroughly.
Boil 200 ml of water.
Add the washed coriander leaves to the boiling water.
Let it boil/steep for 3–4 minutes.
Strain the decoction and drink it on an empty stomach.

recipes.name: Option 1- Makhana Chat

recipes.name: Option 2- Chickpea chat

Now add chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, grated raw mango, jeera powder and pepper powder to it.
Mix well and serve
Option 3- Boiled green gram
Option 4- Boiled Black channa

recipes.name: Option 1 : Lemon Tea
ingredients: - 1 teaspoon loose black tea leaves or 1 tea bag
- 1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice (adjust to taste)
steps: 1. In a small saucepan, bring one cup of water to a boil.
2. Add the black tea leaves or tea bag to the boiling water and let it steep for 2-3 minutes (or according to the package instructions) on medium heat. Steep longer if you prefer a stronger tea.
3. While the tea is steeping, cut a fresh lemon in half and squeeze out one tablespoon of lemon juice. Adjust the amount to suit your taste preference.
4. After steeping, remove the tea leaves or tea bag from the water and discard them.

5. Switch off the Gas. Add the fresh lemon juice to the brewed tea. If you like your tea sweetened, you can add honey or your preferred sweetener at this stage. Stir well until the sweetener dissolves.
6. Pour the lemon tea into your favorite teacup.
7. Optionally, you can garnish the tea with lemon slices and mint leaves for a refreshing touch.
8. Enjoy your hot and revitalizing lemon tea!

recipes.name: Option 2 : LemonGrass Tea
ingredients: - 2 stalks of lemongrass, bruised or chopped
- 1-inch piece of fresh ginger, thinly sliced
steps: 1. In a saucepan, bring 3 cups of water to a boil.
2. Add the lemongrass, ginger slices, and cinnamon stick to the boiling water.
3. Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer for about 10-15 minutes. This will allow the flavors of lemongrass, ginger, and cinnamon to infuse into the water.
4. Switch the Gas off., remove the saucepan from the heat and strain the tea into a teapot or another heat proof container to remove the lemongrass, ginger, and cinnamon pieces.
5. Garnish with a spring of fresh mint if desired.
6. Enjoy your delightful lemongrass, ginger, cinnamon tea!
This aromatic tea is not only delicious but also has potential health benefits from the lemongrass and ginger, making it a fantastic choice for relaxation and rejuvenation.

recipes.name: Option 3 : Tulsi Tea
ingredients: Fresh Tulsi (holy basil) leaves or dried Tulsi leaves
If using fresh Tulsi leaves, wash them thoroughly. If using dried leaves, measure out the desired amount.
Add the Tulsi leaves to the boiling water.
Optionally, add cinnamon or ginger for additional flavor.
Let the mixture simmer for 5-10 minutes to allow the flavors to infuse.
Once the tea has infused, strain out the Tulsi leaves (and any other added ingredients).
Pour the tea into a cup.

Tulsi contains compounds like eugenol, which may help regulate blood sugar levels by enhancing insulin secretion and sensitivity. Consuming Tulsi tea regularly may help stabilize blood glucose levels.

recipes.name: Little Millet / Kodo Millet / Barnyard / Foxtail ( Everyday take 1 millet )
steps: Coarsely grind Any 1 Millet in a mixer jar in pulse mode just for 2 sec.
Wash it with water and drain the water using the filter.
For 1 glass of Millet add 10 glasses of water and let it soak for 8 hours .
Then in the morning take a mud pot, fill it with the same millet soaked water and let it boil.
Once the water starts boiling add the soaked millet and stir well.
Cook till it gets thicker and soft consistency
Switch Off the flame and let it cool for half an hour.
Then cover the entire mud pot with cotton cloth.
Let it ferment for 8 hours
You can add salt after fermentation
Then you can take that kanji for dinner.

recipes.name: Option 1 : Mixed Paruppu thuvaiyal
steps: Dry roast all dal in pan till golden brown
Then add in the mixy jar add grated coconut, dry chilli, garlic, tamarind and salt
Grind well into a thick paste with little water.

recipes.name: Option 2 : Ridge gourd thuvaiyal
steps: Chop the ridge gourd without peeling it.
Add little coconut oil and saute the chopped ridge gourd, grated coconut, dry chilli
Then transfer the sauted ingredients into the mixy jar and some tamarind salt and grind it.

recipes.name: Option 3 : Groundnut thuvaiyal
steps: Dry roast the groundnut and peel out the skin
Dry roast the red chilli and garlic for 30 seconds
Add all the dry roasted ingredients into the mixie jar.
Then add some tamarind and salt and grind well.

recipes.name: Option 4: Vazhaipoo thuvaiyal
steps: Add some water and boil the chopped vazhai poo for 5 mints
Then add little coconut oil and saute coconut, urad dal, red chilli and boiled vazhaipoo just for 30 sec.
Then transfer it to a mixie jar
Add some tamarind & salt grind well

recipes.name: Option 5 : Pirandai thuvaiyal
steps: Clean and chop pirandai into small pieces. Remove the outer skin layer.
Then add some coconut oil and saute dry chilli, onion, bengal gram dal, asafoetida and onion.
Then transfer it to mixy jar and add some tamarind & salt
Then grind well into a smooth paste.

recipes.name: Option - 1: VARAGU IDLI DOSA
steps: 1 cup = 250ml
Varagu/Kodo millet - 1 cup
Round urad dal - 1/4 cup
Methi seeds/Vendhayam - 1/4 tsp
salt and water - as needed
Take all the ingredients given above except salt and wash them twice in water to remove the debris. Soak it together for 4 hours.

Grind them and add enough salt & water. Please do not add more water because they can be easily ground in less water. So use water only when needed. The consistency of batter should be like our regular idli batter.If the batter is too watery, you cannot make idlis. Idli will be flat and sticky. If you add very little water, idli will be hard. So take care while adding water.
Ferment it overnight or minimum 16 hours ( if it is winter). The next morning, the batter would have risen in volume but not doubled.

Stir the batter well with a ladle and make idlis. Steam it in an idli pot for 10 minutes. Check with a back of spoon or using fingers dipped in water. If it comes out clean, idli is cooked. Remove with a spoon and serve hot !
Note
No need to add rice in this recipe.
Do not add more water while grinding.
Idlis come out soft for varagu and dal in 5 :1 ratio. If you want even more softness, use a 4:1 ratio based on the quality of dal.
Adding methi seeds is for softness. Don’t skip it.
Ferment the batter for a minimum of 12 hours. During summer 8 hours is enough.
Use the same cup for measuring all the ingredients.

recipes.name: Option - 2: Kambu/ Bajra/ Pearl millet idli recipe
steps: 1. Wash and soak pearl millet, methi seeds together for 5 hours.
2. Wash and soak urad dal separately in another bowl for 2 hours.
3. Grind urad dal to a smooth paste adding the soaked water.
4. Collect in a bowl and then grind millet, adding enough water.
5. Mix both the batter with your hands and let it ferment overnight. The next day, mix the batter well and make idli.
6. Enjoy with tomato chutney

recipes.name: Option 1 : South Indian Shrimp Soup (Prawn Rasam)
ingredients: - 1 teaspoon rasam powder (South Indian spice blend)
- A small piece of tamarind (soaked in water)
steps: In a pot, bring the cleaned shrimp and 2 cups of water to a gentle simmer. Cook the shrimp for about 2-3 minutes until they turn pink and are cooked through. Remove the shrimp from the water and set them aside.
In the same pot, add chopped onion and sauté until it becomes translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies. Sauté for another minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomato and cook until it becomes soft.
Add turmeric powder and rasam powder. Mix well.
Pour in tamarind water (strained from the soaked tamarind). Adjust the quantity based on your taste preferences.
Add curry leaves and salt. Let the rasam simmer for about 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Add the cooked shrimp back to the pot and let it heat through in the rasam.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves.
Serve the South Indian Shrimp Soup (Prawn Rasam) hot as a tangy and flavorful soup.

recipes.name: Option 2 : Chicken soup
steps: 1. In a pot, add the chicken pieces, onion, garlic, ginger, green chili, and curry leaves. Pour enough water to cover the vegetables and bring it to a boil.
2. Simmer the soup until the chicken is soft and cooked.
3. Add pepper powder and coriander leaves.
4. Add salt to taste, stir well, and serve the Chicken soup hot. It's a vibrant and flavorful option packed with essential nutrients.

recipes.name: Option 3 :Goat leg (Aatukaal) soup
steps: Wash the goat leg thoroughly under cold water.
In a pressure cooker add the washed goat leg
Then add chopped onion, tomato, turmeric powder, ginger garlic paste,salt and water.
Then pressure cook it for 6-8 whistles and switch off the flame.
Then add the pepper and cumin powder and allow it to boil for another 10-15 minutes in low flame.
Ladle the hot goat leg soup into a serving bowl.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves.
Serve it hot
Veg Soup Options

recipes.name: Option 1 :Turmeric Lentil Soup
ingredients: - 1 cup toor dal, rinsed and drained
steps: 1. Add the chopped onions, carrots tomatoes in a pot and add water, make it to boil
2. While boiling,add the minced garlic, ground turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, and ground cinnamon.
3. Add the red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the vegetables and spices.
4. Reduce the heat to a simmer and let the soup cook for about 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and cooked through.
5.Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste..
6. Serve the turmeric lentil soup hot, garnished with chopped fresh coriander .

recipes.name: Option 2 : Tomato and Bell Pepper Soup
steps: 1. In a pot add chopped onion,tomatoes and red bell pepper.
2. Add enough water to cover the ingredients. Bring to a boil and then simmer for a few minutes.
3. Then add paprika turmeric powder, salt, and pepper. Mix well
4. Blend the soup to your desired consistency using an immersion blender or regular blender.

recipes.name: Option 3 : Mixed Vegetable Clear Soup
ingredients: - Assorted vegetables (carrots, beans, peas, corn, etc.), chopped
steps: 1. In a pot, add the chopped vegetables, onion, garlic, ginger, green chilies, and curry leaves. Pour enough water to cover the vegetables and bring it to a boil.
2. Let the soup simmer until the vegetables are cooked but still retain their crunch.
3. Add black pepper powder and salt to taste. Stir well and serve the clear vegetable soup piping hot. It's a nutritious and comforting option for any time of the day.

recipes.name: Option 4 : Mushroom and Fenugreek soup
steps: Add sliced mushrooms and fenugreek leaves in a pot Add water and diced tomatoes.
Let it to boil
Then add ginger, garlic, cumin, and a touch of coconut milk.
Then serve in a bowl with chopped coriander leaves on the topping

recipes.name: Option 5 : Mint and Coriander Soup
steps: In a pot add the chopped onion, garlic, diced potato, ground coriander, turmeric powder, salt, and pepper
Add enough water or vegetable broth to cover the ingredients. Bring to a boil and then simmer until the potato is cooked.
Add fresh mint leaves and coriander leaves. Simmer for a few more minutes.
Blend the soup to a smooth consistency using an immersion blender or regular blender.

recipes.name: Option 6 : Banana stem soup
steps: Clean vazhaithandu by taking out the excess strips around it by peeling off the thick ones. Slice off the thin outer ring (it will be opaque comparatively). Chop roughly into cubes and measure 1 cup.
Gather other ingredients.
Heat a small pressure cooker with coconut oil.
Add fennel seeds, ginger, garlic, chilli and fry for a minute.
Banana stems and little salt. Cook for one more minute.
Add 1 cup water and pressure cook for 3 whistles.
Once done, take out ginger, green chilli. Strain the ingredients for cooling down. Reserve the cooked water.
Once cooled, blend smoothly with little saved water.
Filter through a metal strainer.
Adjust salt.
Heat until it boils and continue simmering for a minute.

recipes.name: Option 7:Broccoli soup
steps: Add broccoli in a pot Add water and diced tomatoes.
Let it to boil
Then add ginger, garlic, cumin, and a touch of coconut milk.
Then serve in a bowl with chopped coriander leaves on the topping

recipeGroups.heading: Fruits
freeText: Do not mix fruits. It is always best to take 1 fruit at a time.
Morning time is best to take fruits . Avoid at night because it may lead to disturbed sleep or may increase cold and mucus formation.
Do not eat fruit along with other foods like rice or vegetables. It will lead to digestion issues.
Diabetes Patients - take fruits as advice by your Doctor or physicians.
In any situation you want to take fruits in between, always have a gap of 1 hr between your fruits and next meals.
